briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon. Welcome to the climate briefing for October 19, 2026. Today, we have received a range of complex news, from reports highlighting the unprecedented severity of climate change, to contradictions in climate actions both domestically and internationally, and various efforts towards carbon neutrality. Notably, the news that 'climate change,' which has been considered the greatest future threat for the past seven years, has been overshadowed by 'AI' raises important questions about how we perceive and respond to the nature of threats [2].

sections.title: 🔴 Deepening Climate Crisis: Unprecedented Changes and Widespread Impacts
sections.content: According to the 2026 State of the Global Climate report, seven out of 16 key climate indicators reached record highs, confirming that the climate crisis is deepening to an unprecedented level [4]. Domestically, compound disasters in the form of heatwaves and torrential rains extending into autumn have prompted warnings that existing summer response methods are insufficient [5], and children's health and right to education are even being threatened by the climate crisis [3]. Internationally, UNEP is urging 'transformative adaptation' to the global drought crisis [6], and rapid ecological changes are being observed, such as the emergence of new islands in the shrinking Caspian Sea and a sharp decline in Antarctic penguin populations [7, 41]. Furthermore, climate change is affecting the quality of major global staple crops, sparking interest in new varieties [34, 37], and reminding us once again that these are issues directly linked to human survival, with California's beaches disappearing and millions facing increased migration risks in South Asia [39, 48].

sections.title: ⚠️ Contradictions in Climate Action and Policy Challenges
sections.content: A domestic public power generation company, advocating for carbon neutrality, faced public criticism for claiming in court that 'cultivated land has increased due to climate change' [1, 32]. This exemplifies the double-standard attitude of corporations, which, while promoting eco-friendliness, allocate only 40% of green finance funds to the renewable energy sector [22]. Domestically, criticisms continue that the '70% self-production of electricity' standard for distributed energy zones and direct power trading standards hinder the expansion of renewable energy [18, 30]. Furthermore, out of a total of 145 trillion won allocated for renewable energy dissemination, 91 trillion won was used for REC support, leading to criticism of high subsidy dependence [19]. Moreover, the increase in solar power generation has led to 6,257 starts and stops of coal-fired power plants over the past five years, incurring restart costs amounting to 840.9 billion won, clearly illustrating the complex challenges in the energy transition process [29].

sections.title: 🌱 Renewable Energy Transition: Progress and Challenges
sections.content: Positive movements towards renewable energy transition are also being observed. The scope of renewable energy has expanded to include sewage and groundwater as hydro-thermal energy [17], and Hyundai E&C is accelerating its entry into overseas markets by intensifying its focus on the Australian power grid and renewable energy market [20, 23]. Domestically, the development of 'transmission-level GFM' technology has commenced in preparation for the 100GW era of renewable energy [24], and energy IT platform companies like Enlighten are supporting efforts to transform renewable energy into an investment driver by offering customized RE100 solutions for businesses [25, 26, 27, 28]. A GlobalData report projects that renewable energy will surpass thermal power generation in South Africa by 2035, demonstrating the potential for transition [31]. However, despite the government's accelerated policies for expanding renewable energy supply, challenges remain, such as the slow development of related insurance products [21].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Societal Efforts and Awareness Expansion Towards Carbon Neutrality
sections.content: Efforts from various sectors of society continue towards transitioning to a carbon-neutral society. CJ Freshway is contributing to carbon neutrality by discovering university students' ideas for reducing food waste [8], and in Gurye County, environmental and ecological education through play for children is gaining attention [11]. The joint resolution declaration on climate action by Seodaemun Eunpyeong Broadcasting [13] and the hosting of 'Noltan Festa' [14] are creating platforms for local communities and families to practice and learn about carbon neutrality. Furthermore, the construction industry is also presenting new paradigms and seeking carbon neutrality solutions [10, 12], with eco-friendly architecture being emphasized from the design stage [15], and the practice of carbon neutrality through waste resource recycling being strongly advocated [16]. These calls for collective action from domestic and international stakeholders underscore the importance of continuous effort and awareness expansion [43].

briefing.closing: Today's briefing has illustrated the deepening reality of the climate crisis and the complex, multifaceted nature of our response to it. Despite the challenges and contradictions we face, we have confirmed that efforts from all sectors of society towards renewable energy transition and carbon neutrality are ongoing. This is a critical time when our responsibility and actions to overcome the climate crisis are more urgent than ever. This concludes today's climate briefing.
